title: AI leads to improved efficiency at SRS’s Salt Waste Processing Facility
summary: The use of artificial intelligence enabled operators of the Savannah River Site’s Salt Waste Processing Facility to make a miniscule mechanical adjustment that resulted in substantially improved efficiency—beyond the design expectations of the facility. The SWPF, which has been operating since 2021, is used to treat salt waste stored in SRS’s radioactive liquid waste tanks. The waste, which originated in chemical separation processes, is pretreated at SWPF to remove cesium and other radionuclides. The pretreated waste is then delivered to the Defense Waste Processing Facility for vitrification.

title: Extending the Life of Aging Nuclear Assets Without Major Replacement
summary: More than two-thirds of the U.S. nuclear fleet has now been operating for over 40 years, and many plants are pursuing subsequent license renewal to continue generating carbon-free electricity well into the 2050s. As facilities age, maintaining components affected by corrosion/erosion mechanisms, including flow accelerated corrosion (FAC) in particular, has become an increasingly important part of long-term operation. Cross-under piping, feedwater systems and steam turbine components are particularly vulnerable. High-velocity wet steam gradually removes the protective oxide layer from carbon steel, leading to wall thinning, erosion and reduced structural margin. Left unmanaged, these degradation mechanisms can result in costly repairs, extended outages and, ultimately, replacement of major components.

title: IAEA General Conference kicks off with opening remarks from DG Grossi
summary: When the International Atomic Energy Agency held its first General Conference in 1956, the global organization had only 56 member states. As of its 70th General Conference this week, the number is up to 182. IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi was quick to mention this updated count during an opening statement that kickstarted the five-day event in Vienna, Austria, this morning. He also noted that nearly 4,000 people were expected to attend the General Conference.
